hero.heading: Generations Custom Auto & Collision, a cost model sent for correction
hero.caption: Built October 4, 2026, from generationscollisionservices.com, the shop's own social pages, the industry's billing survey, and federal data. Every number is labeled: published, federal, or our assumption. The assumptions are sliders; move them and the number moves.
hero.liveCaption: The model's estimate, on the assumptions you have set below
hero.subline: (exact: $2,936 and $67,742) Under $5,000 a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000, above it to the nearest $5,000; the exact figures govern.

model.heading: Move our assumptions
model.intro: Each slider is one of the assumptions in our letter, set to the range we wrote down. If you know a figure, narrow its range, or close both handles on the exact number. The estimate above then follows your figures instead of ours. Tap a figure to type it exactly.

volume.label: Jobs you complete in a year
volume.caption: Optional. Type your volume and every dollar figure on this page scales to your year. Leave it empty and the model stays per hundred jobs.

sliders.label: Share of jobs that are custom or restoration
Unbilled hours on one custom or restoration job
sliders.basis: The hours that run over a quote given once. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Share of jobs that are collision
sliders.basis: Held at 70 percent in our model; move it if your mix differs. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

sliders.label: Not-included operations performed and never billed, per collision job
Months between estimate and parts order
sliders.basis: Half a month to two months, about two to eight weeks. Assumed, printed to be corrected [[ASSUMED]].

constants.text: Federal series: BLS producer price index, motor vehicle parts (WPU1412), 145.456 in October 2025 to 149.359 in August 2026, its latest published month: up 2.7 percent over ten months, 0.27 percent per month [[BENCHMARK]]. The model applies it only across the weeks between estimate and parts order. Next release October 15, 2026; this page changes with it.

terms.label: Unbilled hours on custom and restoration
Parts drift between estimate and order

model.formulaText: Moved per 100 jobs = 100 × custom share × unbilled hours per custom job × hourly rate + 100 × collision share × unbilled operations per collision job × value per operation + 100 × parts per repair × months of lag × (149.359 ÷ 145.456 minus 1) ÷ 10
model.plainText: In words, the hours custom and restoration work absorb beyond its quote, plus the not-included collision operations performed and never written, plus what parts prices add while an estimate waits for its parts order.
model.callout: What nobody counts at a shop that does four kinds of work is which kind pays for the others. A collision repair is quoted, supplemented, and paid by an insurer who argues every line; a restoration is quoted once and finished when it is finished; a bus is neither. The hours that run over on a custom job appear on no invoice. The not-included operations on a collision job, by the industry's own survey of 473 shops, are paid most of the time when written and never paid by the one shop in five that never writes them. And a year's backlog of repaints is either your best customers waiting or your best margin waiting.

smallRound.note: Under $5,000, a figure rounds to the nearest $1,000.

respect.heading: What you already show in the open
paragraphs: Coach work on buggies and wagons in 1928, the first wrecker in the county, and ninety-eight years later one of the oldest single-family body shops in the state, with you and Michelle at the desk [[OBSERVED]].
Collision on everything from cars to school buses and box trucks. Dent repair done in-house. Restoration and custom work for the old classics. A wrecker that answers at night [[OBSERVED]].
A customer on your own page who waited a year for a small window to get a truck repainted, and was glad to [[OBSERVED]].

proposal.heading: What we propose
proposal.lead: The proposal: the four-line count (collision, commercial, custom, towing: hours worked against billed, operations performed against billed, backlog in days), the decision page in your words, and the first month run on it, counted; fixed fee between $1,500 and $2,500; read-only; no customer or vehicle identity leaves the building.

ledger.title: What a quarter of the four-line count looks like
ledger.label: Illustrative, not Generations data
ledger.note: An illustrative quarter, priced at $72 an hour. Towing is billed per call at flat fees, so no hours are counted for it. Every line and figure is invented to show the format.

proposal.promise: If your records show our printed range overstated your exposure, our findings letter says so in those words.
